'''Melnea's World''' was a gloomy and [[Swamp/Legends|swampy]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] located in the [[Melnea's World system/Legends|Melnea's World system]], a part of the [[Arkanis sector/Legends|Arkanis sector]] in [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]] portion of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. It was situated on the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] known as the [[Cranan-Excarga Route/Legends|Cranan-Excarga Route]], which linked it to the [[Cranan system/Legends|Cranan system]] as well as the [[Excarga system/Legends|Excarga system]]<ref name="TEA" /> of the [[Herios sector/Legends|Herios sector]].<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref>

Melnea's World was [[Colonist/Legends|settled]] by [[Miner/Legends|miners]] from the [[Tatoo system/Legends|Tatoo system's]] planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] after [[Mining/Legends|mining]] efforts on that world had proved fruitless.<ref name="TEA" /> It shared its name with [[Melnea Arnthout]], the leader of a group of miner colonists who established the [[City/Legends|settlement]] of [[Bestine (city)/Legends|Bestine]] on Tatooine.<ref name="Secrets">''[[Secrets of Tatooine]]''</ref> The mines on Melnea's World also proved to be poor, however, and in the [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] preceding<ref name="TEA" /> [[43 ABY]],<ref name="Date">The main section of ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', which describes Melnea's World, ends with a mention of [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke]] and [[Ben Skywalker]]'s journey across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], the beginning of which is depicted in ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Outcast]]''. ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of that novel to [[43 ABY]].</ref> the world gained more notability as a [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] hideout.<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
Melnea's World was mentioned in the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]], which placed it in grid square R-16.<ref name="TEA" />
